articles.title: Enough Energy, but Rising Grid Imports
articles.titleZh: 电量够用，怎么又买起了电
articles.summary: The university open-day plan still has enough energy over the whole day, but thick cloud arrives early just as the arena starts equipment tests, leaving local instantaneous power insufficient. The public grid immediately supplies the net difference and the battery control system rapidly increases discharge. Mia then delays one flexible load to avoid the extra imports its scheduled start would require and preserve battery energy for later in the evening.
articles.summaryZh: 大学开放日原计划的全天电量仍有余量，但厚云提前到来、体育馆又提前启动设备，使某一时刻的本地功率不足。公共电网立即承担净差额，电池控制系统自动快速放电；米娅随后延后一组可调负荷，避免原计划启动造成的额外外购并保留电池余量。
storyParagraphs: On the evening of the university open day, Mia is in the campus energy room. The arena lights come on early and cloud arrives ahead of the forecast; a new rise appears in grid imports on her screen. The dining hall and exhibition spaces will also get busy at 18:00. She checks the daily plan again: local generation and the stored energy scheduled for use had been enough in total. Volunteers are already handing out visitor badges outside. There is no time to rearrange the whole event.

At 17:50, the arena begins its lighting and sound tests as thick cloud rapidly reduces solar output. The campus remains connected to the public grid, which supplies power that local sources cannot provide; the enabled battery controls also increase discharge within seconds. The lights stay on, but power she had planned to buy less of is now arriving from outside.

A colleague asks, “Isn’t there still energy in the battery?” Mia opens its status panel. About 240 kWh of usable energy is available at that moment, but the battery's maximum discharge power is 120 kW. The first number says how much usable energy remains; the second says how much power the battery can deliver at one instant. The automatic controls have already raised battery output within its permitted range, yet the campus still needs the public grid for the remaining power. She tries raising the requested output, but the interface keeps it within the equipment limit. Having more energy left cannot raise that instantaneous limit. If high discharge continues, less battery energy will remain for later changes in the evening.

Mia leaves the arena alone. A 40 kW cold-store compressor group is waiting for its next timed start. The person responsible confirms that this cycle can be deferred within the permitted temperature range, so she changes its start time. At the originally scheduled moment, the campus does not add that 40 kW load and avoids the corresponding extra grid import it would have needed. The cold store still has to complete the cooling cycle later; she moves the work to a period when solar output is expected to recover.

As the cloud thins, solar output gradually recovers. Mia lets the compressor group start in its revised time window, while the battery control system reduces discharge. At 18:00 the arena opens on schedule and the entrance lightbox has stayed on throughout. Before handover, she writes the two units separately in the log: the day's plan and remaining battery energy are recorded in kWh, while load, generation, and battery output at a given instant are recorded in kW.
storyParagraphsZh: 大学开放日傍晚，米娅守在校园能源值班室。体育馆比计划早开了灯，窗外的云又比预报早到，她的屏幕上忽然多出一截外购电。18:00食堂和展厅还要同时忙起来。她翻回日计划：本地发电加上当天安排使用的储能，累计电量本来足够。门外志愿者正在发参观牌，已经没有时间重排整场活动。
17:50，体育馆开始灯光和音响测试时，厚云让太阳能输出迅速下降。校园仍与公共电网相连，外部电网补上本地不足的功率；已经启用的电池控制也在几秒内增加放电。灯没有灭，但她原来准备少买的电，现在正从外面送进来。

同事看着外购曲线问：“电池里不是还有电吗？”米娅打开电池状态：此刻可用能量约240 kWh，但设备最大放电功率是120 kW。前一个数字说的是还存有多少电，后一个数字说的是这一刻最多能送出多大功率。自动控制已经把电池提高到允许范围，校园仍需要从外部电网取得剩余功率。她试着提高设定，界面仍把输出限制在设备允许范围内；再多的剩余电量也不能把这一刻的上限推高。若一直保持高输出，电池留给晚间后续变化的余量也会越来越少。
米娅没有去动体育馆。冷库那组40 kW压缩机正等着下一次定时启动，负责人确认可以在允许温度范围内把这一轮推迟。她改了启动时间。原定时刻到了，校园没有再增加这40 kW负荷，也就少了原本需要外部电网补上的这一截。冷库后来仍得做完这轮制冷；她只是把工作移到太阳能有望恢复的时段。
云层变薄后，太阳能逐渐恢复。米娅让那组压缩机按新的时段启动，电池控制系统也降低输出。18:00体育馆照常开门，入口灯箱一直亮着。交班前，她在记录上把两种单位分开写：日计划和电池剩余量用kWh，某一时刻的负荷、发电和电池输出用kW。
explanationParagraphs: Grid balancing requires electricity supply and demand to remain matched during real-time operation. kW describes power at a particular moment, while kWh describes accumulated energy over time; a sufficient daily energy budget does not guarantee sufficient power at every instant.

The battery has about 240 kWh of usable energy and a maximum output of 120 kW. In an idealized constant-output model, 240 ÷ 120 = 2 hours at that power; remaining energy still cannot overcome the power limit. Deferring the inactive 40 kW device avoids demand that would otherwise be added then.
explanationParagraphsZh: 电网平衡要求发电与用电在实时运行中持续匹配。kW描述某一时刻的功率，kWh描述一段时间累计的电量；全天能量预算充足不能保证任一时刻功率充足。
本例电池可用能量约240 kWh，最大输出120 kW。在理想简化模型中，持续以120 kW输出约能用240÷120＝2小时；有电可用却仍不能突破功率上限。延后未启动的40 kW设备，则避免了当时本来会增加的需求。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用虚构并网校园说明电网平衡的一个入门区别：累计电量够用，并不代表每个时刻的功率都匹配。短时变化必须由电网、快速储能或其他可行调节立即承接；人工随后可以重新安排持续供给与可调负荷。本篇不是完整电网频率控制案例。
articles.overall: This fictional grid-connected campus illustrates one introductory distinction in grid balancing: having enough accumulated energy over a day does not mean power is matched at every instant. Short-term changes must be met immediately by the wider grid, fast storage, or other feasible responses; human operators can then rearrange sustained supply and flexible demand. This is not a complete example of grid-frequency control.

moduleZh.intro: 用校园并网这一缩小场景区分“今天总共有多少电”和“这一刻需要多少功率”。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 全天电量有余量，为什么傍晚仍会突然增加外购功率
diagramSteps: 日计划中累计可用电量足够，但每个时段仍需安排相应功率
厚云降低本地太阳能，同时体育馆提前启动使瞬时负荷升高
公共电网立即承担净差额，电池自动控制在几秒内提高放电功率
电池仍受120 kW最大输出约束，240 kWh可用能量不能解除功率限制
米娅延后尚未启动的40 kW负荷，避免这一时刻继续增加需求；太阳能恢复后再安排启动
diagramStepNotes: 日累计电量预算不能代替实时功率平衡。
条件变化来自天气和活动时序，而不是人物忘记基本常识。
物理平衡由并网系统和自动响应即时维持，人工不让明显缺口悬空等待。
240 kWh÷120 kW＝2小时是理想持续输出尺度，不是实际续航承诺；能量够也不能超过120 kW上限。
延后未启动设备是避免未来增量，不是从已测负荷中减去40 kW；冷库后来仍需完成制冷。
mapping: 开放日18:00开门 → 人物必须维持的真实校园任务。
抬高的外购功率曲线 → 本地供需瞬时变化的可见结果。
240 kWh与120 kW → 储能能量容量和功率能力的区别。
延后的40 kW压缩机 → 避免计划启动时再增加需求，而非取消后续制冷。
moduleZh.boundary: 本例假定并网线路能承接差额，设备与冷库仍在允许运行范围内。校园安排展示功率与累计电量的区别，并不代替系统级频率、线路和备用管理。可用能量与最大输出各有限制，2小时只是假定恒定输出的简化计算；推迟制冷也不是免去制冷。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果一块电池还有300 kWh可用能量，但最大只能输出50 kW，它为什么不能单独立刻承担新增100 kW负荷？

module.intro: Use a small grid-connected campus example to separate “how much energy is available today” from “how much power is needed right now.”
module.diagramTitle: If the Daily Energy Budget Has Headroom, Why Can Grid Imports Still Jump in the Evening?
diagramSteps: Daily available energy is sufficient, but power still has to be scheduled for each period
Thick cloud reduces local solar output while the arena starts early and raises instantaneous demand
The public grid immediately supplies the net difference while battery controls increase discharge within seconds
The battery remains limited to 120 kW maximum output even with about 240 kWh of usable energy available
Mia defers the not-yet-started 40 kW load, avoiding an additional demand increase, and starts it later after solar output recovers
diagramStepNotes: A daily accumulated energy budget cannot replace real-time power balance.
The change comes from weather and activity timing, not from a character failing to understand basic arithmetic.
Physical balance is maintained immediately by the grid connection and automatic response rather than leaving an obvious deficit waiting for manual action.
240 kWh ÷ 120 kW = 2 hours is an idealized constant-output timescale, not a runtime promise. Available energy cannot overcome the 120 kW limit.
Deferring an inactive device avoids a future increase; it does not subtract 40 kW from measured demand. Cooling is still completed later.
mapping: 18:00 open-day opening → the campus task Mia must keep on schedule.
Raised import-power curve → the visible result of an instantaneous local supply-demand change.
240 kWh and 120 kW → the distinction between battery energy capacity and power capability.
Deferred 40 kW compressor group → an avoided scheduled demand increase, with cooling still required later.
module.boundary: This example assumes that the grid connection can supply the difference and equipment and cold storage stay within operating limits. Campus scheduling illustrates power versus accumulated energy, not full frequency, network, or reserve management. Usable energy and maximum power impose separate limits; two hours is a simplified constant-output calculation, and deferred cooling is not canceled cooling.
module.reflection: If a battery still has 300 kWh of usable energy but can output only 50 kW, why can it not by itself immediately cover a new 100 kW load?

referencesZh.use: 支持电力系统需要实时平衡供需，并通过可行的发电和需求调整应对运行变化，同时受实际运行和位置约束。

articles.title: The Towel That Could Not Go Upstairs
articles.summary: The hotel must decide whether to replace two more dryers. The new machine uses only 4.8 kWh in its first run, but the towels are still damp, so that result cannot be used to compare efficiency. Su Rui then repeats the test with 12 kg dry weight of the same towels, similar post-spin moisture conditions, and the same final dryness requirement: the old dryer uses about 9 kWh and the new one about 6 kWh, but the new machine takes longer per load.
articles.summaryZh: 酒店要决定是否再换两台烘干机。新机器第一次只用了4.8 kWh，但毛巾仍有潮气，这次结果不能用来比较效率。苏芮随后用干重相同的12 kg毛巾、相近脱水后含水状态和同一最终干燥要求重新测试：旧机约9 kWh，新机约6 kWh，但新机每批更慢。
storyParagraphs: Housekeeping will collect the white towels at three. The new dryer Su Rui is testing has stopped, but the towels still feel damp; two empty carts wait at the laundry room door. The owner bought one machine for a trial, hoping to replace the other two before winter. With the job still unfinished, she has a more urgent question than the electricity bill: can these towels go upstairs?

The meter has risen by only 4.8 kWh. Su Rui has just photographed the number when her colleague pulls out a towel. “This load can’t go upstairs yet.” It is not dripping, but it is still noticeably damp. Su Rui deletes the good-news message she has started and turns the cart back toward the dryer. The floors are waiting for dry towels; that low meter reading cannot finish the job for her.

The next day, Su Rui repeats the comparison. She prepares 12 kg dry weight of the same type of towels for each machine, runs both batches through the same washing and spin cycle, checks that their wet weights before entering the drums are similar, and requires both machines to reach the same dryness accepted by housekeeping before the test ends. The old machine finishes first and uses about 9 kWh. The new one runs for more than ten minutes longer and uses about 6 kWh when it reaches the same dryness requirement.

This time both carts go to the same folding table for the same colleague to check. Su Rui records energy use beside finishing time. When the owner comes for the purchasing sheet, she is less eager to report good news than she was yesterday. He points to “new machine slower.” “Will it keep up with those carts of sheets at the weekend?” She opens the weekend schedule and puts the purchasing sheet underneath it.

Before three, both trial loads are back on the guest floors. Su Rui keeps the first “4.8 kWh” note in the folder, now marked “not dry yet.” On the purchasing sheet, 9 kWh and 6 kWh sit side by side. Beneath “same load, same dryness” is another line: the extra time taken by the new machine.
storyParagraphsZh: 下午三点，客房部就要来收白毛巾。苏芮试用的新烘干机已经停了，毛巾摸着却还有潮气，两辆空推车仍等在洗衣房门口。老板先买一台让她试，原本想在冬天前把另外两台也换掉；这批活还没交出去，她就得回答一个比电费更急的问题：毛巾能不能上楼？
电表只增加了4.8 kWh。苏芮刚把数字拍下来，折毛巾的同事就抽出一条递回来：“这批还不能上架。”毛巾没有滴水，却仍带着明显潮气。苏芮把刚写好的报喜消息删掉，推车掉头，回到烘干机旁。楼层等的是干毛巾，电表上的这个低数字暂时交不了差。
第二天，苏芮重新做比较。她给两台机器各准备干重12 kg的同款毛巾，让它们经过同一洗涤和脱水程序，确认进滚筒前的湿重相近，再要求两边都达到客房部接受的同一干燥程度才结束。旧机器先完成，用电约9 kWh；新机器多转了十几分钟，达到同样干燥要求时用了约6 kWh。
这次两车毛巾都推到同一个折叠台，由同一位同事检查。苏芮把耗电和完成时间写在一起，老板来拿采购表时，她没有像昨天那样急着报好消息。他指着“新机较慢”问：“周末那几车床单，能赶上吗？”苏芮翻开周末的排班页，先把采购表压在下面。
下午三点前，两批测试毛巾都回到楼层。苏芮把第一张“4.8 kWh”记录留在夹子里，旁边注明“还没烘干”。采购表上，9 kWh和6 kWh并排写着；“同样一批、同样干燥”下面，还有一行新机多用的时间。
explanationParagraphs: Energy efficiency concerns providing the same or a comparable service with less energy, rather than simply reducing output. Here the dry towel mass, initial moisture condition, and final dryness requirement are held comparable before energy use is compared.

In this comparable trial, the old dryer uses about 9 kWh and the new one about 6 kWh. The saving is (9 − 6) ÷ 9 ≈ 33%, or roughly one-third. The new machine is still slower. The first 4.8 kWh run did not complete the same task and cannot enter this comparison; other loads and environments may give different results.
explanationParagraphsZh: 能源效率关注用更少能源提供相同或可比服务，而不是单纯减少输出。本例先固定干毛巾重量、初始含水状态和最终干燥要求，再比较能耗。
本次可比试验里，旧机约9 kWh、新机约6 kWh，节省比例为（9－6）÷9＝约33%，也就是约三分之一。新机仍更慢；第一批的4.8 kWh并未完成相同任务，不能算入这个比较，其他负载和环境也可能得到不同结果。
articles.overallZh: 本篇讲能源效率的一个基本判断：只有在提供同等服务、比较条件可比时，较少能源输入才支持效率提高。本次虚构试验中，新机把同样12 kg干毛巾烘到同一要求时由约9 kWh降到约6 kWh，但耗时更长；这不能自动推广成整个品牌或所有使用条件的结论。

moduleZh.intro: 先确认两台机器完成的是同一个烘干任务，再比较为这项服务各自用了多少电。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 先把毛巾烘到同样干，再比较电量
diagramSteps: 第一次新机只用4.8 kWh，但毛巾未达到客房部的同一干燥要求
第二次各取干重12 kg同款毛巾，并采用相同洗涤和脱水流程
确认进入滚筒前含水状态相近，并以同一最终干燥要求为终点
旧机完成任务约用9 kWh，新机完成同一任务约用6 kWh
同时记录新机多用的十几分钟，作为采购决定中的另一项代价
diagramStepNotes: 第一批服务量不同，因此4.8 kWh不是可比效率证据。
12 kg指毛巾干重，不是吸水后的滚筒总重量。
比较条件无需绝对完全相同，但关键服务和主要初始条件应尽量可比。
6相对9约减少三分之一，只适用于这次相同服务试验。
单批效率改善不等于所有工况、全年总能耗或整个品牌都得到同样结果。
mapping: 退回的潮毛巾 → 较低能耗背后服务没有完成。
干重12 kg → 两次可比任务的共同服务量。
9 kWh与6 kWh → 同一服务下的能源输入差异。
多出的十几分钟 → 省电之外需要承担的设备占用代价。
moduleZh.boundary: 效率比较必须基于可比服务和条件。减少产量、亮度、温度控制或干燥程度而少用电，不能自动叫效率提高。本篇只有一次虚构设备比较，不能据此推广到不同负载、环境、维护状态或整个品牌；绝对总用能还会受到实际使用量影响。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果另一台烘干机只用了5 kWh，但最后毛巾比客房要求更潮，为什么这个5 kWh不能直接拿来和本篇的6 kWh比较效率？

referencesZh.citation: U.S. Department of Energy. Energy Efficiency vs. Energy Intensity. Official definition page.
referencesZh.use: 支持以较少能源输入提供相同服务属于效率改善，并提醒结构、行为和服务量变化会使总体能耗指标不再是直接的设备效率比较。

articles.overall: This article introduces a basic test of energy efficiency: lower energy input supports an efficiency improvement only when the service provided and the comparison conditions are comparable. In this fictional trial, the new dryer reduces energy use from about 9 kWh to about 6 kWh while drying the same 12 kg dry weight of towels to the same requirement, but it takes longer. That result cannot automatically be generalized to an entire brand or every operating condition.

module.intro: First establish that both dryers complete the same drying task, then compare how much electricity each uses to provide that service.
module.diagramTitle: Dry the Towels Equally Before Comparing Energy
diagramSteps: The first new-dryer run uses only 4.8 kWh, but the towels do not reach the same housekeeping dryness requirement
For the second test, prepare 12 kg dry weight of the same towels and use the same washing and spin process
Confirm similar moisture conditions before drying and use the same final dryness requirement as the endpoint
The old dryer completes the task using about 9 kWh; the new dryer completes the same task using about 6 kWh
Record the extra ten-plus minutes taken by the new dryer as another cost in the purchasing decision
diagramStepNotes: The first load provides a different level of service, so 4.8 kWh is not comparable efficiency evidence.
The 12 kg refers to dry towel mass, not the total wet mass entering the drum.
Comparison conditions do not need to be perfectly identical, but the key service and major starting conditions should be sufficiently comparable.
The reduction from 9 to 6 is about one-third and applies only to this same-service trial.
A single-load efficiency improvement does not imply the same result for every operating condition, annual energy use, or the entire brand.
mapping: Returned damp towel → lower energy use accompanied by an unfinished service.
12 kg dry weight → the common service quantity in the comparable trial.
9 kWh and 6 kWh → different energy inputs for the same service.
Extra ten-plus minutes → the equipment-time cost that accompanies the energy saving.
module.boundary: Efficiency comparisons require comparable service and conditions. Using less electricity by reducing output, brightness, temperature control, or dryness does not automatically mean higher efficiency. This article contains only one fictional equipment comparison and cannot be generalized to different loads, environments, maintenance states, or an entire brand. Absolute total energy use also depends on how much the equipment is actually used.
module.reflection: If another dryer uses only 5 kWh but leaves the towels wetter than housekeeping requires, why can that 5 kWh not be compared directly with the 6 kWh result in this article?

references.citation: U.S. Department of Energy. Energy Efficiency vs. Energy Intensity. Official definition page.
references.use: Supports the idea that providing the same service with less energy input represents an efficiency improvement, while structural, behavioral, and service-level changes can make aggregate energy-use measures unsuitable as direct equipment-efficiency comparisons.

articles.summaryZh: 许清想用白天存下来的太阳能，撑过学习室的晚间活动。开始前，清洁人员推来一台设备，也想趁这段时间一起用电。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区学习室晚上有一场两小时的语言交换活动。许清准备让具备独立供电能力的储能系统承担这两个小时的灯光和屏幕：太阳已经落下，晚上也没有其他并供电源。活动开始前，清洁人员推来一台功率为1千瓦（kW）、需要连续运行一小时的设备：“能不能顺便开着？这样明早不用再跑一趟。”
白天，屋顶太阳能满足当时用电后，在同一交流侧计量点还有6千瓦时（kWh）的可利用电量。储能的可用电量当时已到允许下限，充电时间和功率都足够。许清把其中5 kWh交流电充入储能；按这次设定的80%往返效率，之后整次放电可向交流负载交付4 kWh。另有1 kWh白天富余电没有充进储能。
许清再看逆变器参数：持续额定输出是2 kW。灯光和屏幕本身就持续需要2 kW；清洁设备若同时运行，持续需求会变成3 kW，超过这次已知的持续额定能力。她不能按这套额定能力把两项任务同时安排进去，便把清洁设备的插头卷回机器旁：“今晚先不接它。”
活动开始后，储能稳定承担2 kW基本负载。许清这次把全部4 kWh可交付电量都安排给活动，没有另留备用量。一小时后用掉2 kWh，还剩2 kWh；第二小时再用掉余下的电，散场时这次可交付电量刚好用完。
活动散场后，屏幕熄灭，清洁设备仍停在墙边。许清给第二天的清洁重新排了时段，锁上学习室的门。次日早晨，场地方确认正常电网供电已经恢复，清洁人员回来，用这段供电时间完成了工作；为了这一小时，他们多跑了一趟。
articles.overallZh: 储能可以把白天富余电移到夜晚，但可交付能量和持续输出功率是不同约束。本例的4 kWh刚好供2 kW基本负载运行两小时；若另加1 kW清洁设备运行一小时，即使持续输出能力足够，所需总电量也会增至5 kWh。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例的6 kWh富余量和5 kWh充电量都在交流侧计量。储能从允许的可用下限开始充电，输入5 kWh；假定交流输入到交流输出的往返效率为80%，之后整次可交付5×0.80=4 kWh。白天另有1 kWh富余电未充入；从5变4所损失的1 kWh是另一笔能量，不能混为一谈。4 kWh已计入该往返损失，放电时不再重复乘80%。
4 kWh是可交付的能量总量，2 kW是本例给出的持续额定输出能力。假定这次充电后的4 kWh全部可交付、额定工况稳定输出且不另留余量，2 kW运行两小时用去4 kWh；再让1 kW设备运行一小时，合计需5 kWh。若同时运行，连续需求3 kW也超过2 kW的持续额定能力。短时过载能力要另查设备规格，不能仅由持续额定值推断。

moduleZh.intro: 先区分白天充入与夜间可交付的交流电量，再分别核对持续输出能力和整段任务需要的能量。

kW描述功率；kWh是功率随时间累计的能量。清洁的一小时是本教学例的任务条件。
这里比较持续额定能力，不根据它推断短时过载能力；该能力须另查实际设备规格。
基本任务2×2=4 kWh；若额外清洁1×1=1 kWh，合计5 kWh。4÷2=2小时还假设这次充电后的4 kWh全部可交付、稳定输出且无额外备用余量。
mapping: 白天6 kWh交流侧富余光伏 → 与夜间负荷时间错开的可利用发电。
5 kWh充入、4 kWh可交付 → 计入往返损耗后的跨时间能量转移。
逆变器2 kW持续额定输出 → 持续运行负载的功率能力约束。

moduleZh.boundary: 这是统一到交流侧的简化教学模型，不提供真实离网系统设计、布线、安全操作或设备选型。实际可用容量、充放电效率、逆变器功率、温度、寿命、剩余荷电状态和保护策略都会影响结果。若夜间存在可用电网或其他允许并供的电源，3 kW总负载可以有不同的供能组合；本故事特意选择储能独立承担基本负载，以突出能量容量与功率容量的区别。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果把逆变器持续额定输出提高到3 kW，但仍只有4 kWh可交付电量，能否同时完成2 kW基本负载两小时和1 kW清洁任务一小时？为什么？

articles.title: Another Trip Tomorrow?
articles.summary: Xu Qing wants stored daytime solar energy to power an evening event at the study room. Just before it starts, the cleaning staff wheel in a machine they hope to run at the same time.
storyParagraphs: The community study room has a two-hour language-exchange event that evening. Xu Qing plans to use a storage system capable of standalone operation for the lights and screens: the sun has set and no other power source is available in parallel. Just before the event, the cleaning staff wheel over a 1-kilowatt (kW) machine that needs to run continuously for an hour. “Can we run it at the same time? Then we won’t have to come back tomorrow morning.”

During the day, after meeting the current load, rooftop solar has 6 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of usable surplus measured at the same AC-side point. The storage system has reached its permitted usable lower limit, and charging time and power are sufficient. Xu Qing sends 5 kWh of AC electricity into storage. At the assumed 80% round-trip efficiency, the complete later discharge can deliver 4 kWh to AC loads. Another 1 kWh of daytime surplus does not enter storage.

Xu Qing checks the inverter rating: its continuous rated output is 2 kW. The lights and screens already need a continuous 2 kW; running the cleaner alongside them would require a continuous 3 kW, beyond the specified continuous rating. She cannot schedule both tasks together on that rated capability, so she coils the cleaner’s plug beside the machine. “Not tonight.”

The event begins with storage steadily supplying the 2 kW basic load. Xu Qing allocates the full 4 kWh deliverable amount to the event, with no separate reserve. After one hour it has delivered 2 kWh and has 2 kWh left; the second hour uses the remainder, exhausting this deliverable amount as the event ends.

After the event, the screen goes dark and the cleaning machine remains by the wall. Xu Qing schedules the work for the following day and locks the study room. The next morning, the venue confirms that normal grid power is available again, and the cleaners return to finish the job during that supply period. The one-hour task has cost them an extra trip.
articles.overall: Storage can shift surplus electricity from day to evening, but deliverable energy and continuous output power are separate constraints. Here 4 kWh is just enough for the 2 kW basic load for two hours. Adding a 1 kW cleaner for one hour would raise total energy demand to 5 kWh even if sufficient continuous output power were available.
explanationParagraphs: The 6 kWh surplus and 5 kWh charging input are measured on the AC side. Storage starts charging from its permitted usable lower limit. At an assumed 80% round-trip efficiency from AC input to AC output, the 5 kWh input yields 5×0.80=4 kWh for the complete later discharge. Another 1 kWh of daytime surplus was not charged; the 1 kWh lost between the 5 kWh input and 4 kWh output is a different quantity. The deliverable 4 kWh already includes this loss and is not multiplied by 80% again during discharge.

The 4 kWh is total deliverable energy; 2 kW is the continuous rated output specified here. Assuming the 4 kWh from this charge is fully deliverable, steady rated output and no separate reserve, 2 kW for two hours uses 4 kWh. A 1 kW machine for another hour raises total demand to 5 kWh. If run alongside the basic load, the continuous demand of 3 kW also exceeds the 2 kW continuous rating. Short-duration overload capability requires separate specifications and cannot be inferred from that rating alone.

module.intro: Distinguish AC energy charged in the daytime from deliverable energy at night, then check continuous rated output and total task energy separately.
module.diagramTitle: Why Is Energy Just Sufficient for the Basic Event but Not for an Additional Cleaning Task?
diagramSteps: From 6 kWh AC-side daytime surplus, charge 5 kWh into storage starting at its permitted lower limit
At 80% round-trip efficiency, the complete discharge can deliver 4 kWh to AC loads
The evening basic load requires 2 kW for two hours; the cleaner would need another 1 kW for one hour
Running them together would require a continuous 3 kW, above the inverter’s 2 kW continuous rating
Defer cleaning: the basic task uses the 4 kWh, and the cleaner returns when grid power is available next morning
diagramStepNotes: The 6 and 5 kWh are both AC-side quantities. The other 1 kWh surplus was not charged; its later use is not assumed.
The difference between 5 kWh input and 4 kWh deliverable is 1 kWh of round-trip loss, distinct from the uncharged 1 kWh; do not multiply the 4 by efficiency again.
kW describes power, while kWh is energy accumulated over time. The one-hour cleaning duration is an assumption in this teaching case.
This compares continuous ratings; short-duration overload capability is not inferred and requires actual equipment specifications.

The basic task uses 2×2=4 kWh. Adding cleaning uses 1×1=1 kWh, totaling 5 kWh. The 4÷2=2 h duration also assumes the 4 kWh from this charge is fully deliverable, steady output and no separate reserve.
mapping: 6 kWh of AC-side daytime surplus solar → usable generation occurring at a different time from the evening load.
5 kWh charged and 4 kWh deliverable → energy shifted across time after round-trip loss.
2 kW continuous inverter rating → a power constraint on loads running continuously.
Deferring the 1 kW, one-hour cleaning task → changing timing in response to both continuous power and total energy constraints.
module.boundary: This is a simplified teaching model using an AC-side accounting basis. It is not a guide to real standalone-system design, wiring, safety operation, or equipment selection. Actual usable capacity, charging and discharging efficiency, inverter power, temperature, ageing, remaining state of charge, and protection strategies can all change real performance. If a usable grid connection or another permitted parallel source were available at night, the 3 kW total load could be supplied in a different combination. This story deliberately has storage independently support the basic load in order to isolate the distinction between energy capacity and power capacity.
module.reflection: If the inverter’s continuous rating rose to 3 kW but only 4 kWh remained deliverable, could it power the 2 kW basic task for two hours and a 1 kW cleaner for one hour? Why or why not?

references.use: Supports the time mismatch between solar generation and electricity demand, the use of storage to shift energy from one period to another, and the distinction among energy capacity, power capacity, and conversion losses. It is not used as a performance guarantee for the fictional study room or any specific storage device.

references.use: Supports distinguishing power capacity from energy capacity and using energy capacity divided by rated power to understand theoretical duration at that output. Historical equipment statistics and examples are not treated as real parameters for the fictional system in this story.

references.use: Supports understanding round-trip efficiency as the ratio of electricity delivered from storage to electricity put into storage, and supports the principle that charging and discharging involve energy losses. The 80% value in this story is a fictional teaching assumption and does not represent all real storage systems.

articles.title: Wait for the Yellow-Dot Box
articles.summary: On a gift-box packaging line, the labeling head and inspection camera are separated by several box positions. After Qiao Wei makes the first adjustment to the right, the next camera image still shows a box labeled before that adjustment, so she adjusts right once more. When the boxes corresponding to the two adjustments later reach the camera, the label moves from near the center to too far right. She then marks the first box after an adjustment with a yellow dot and waits until that box reaches the camera before deciding what to do next.
articles.summaryZh: 礼盒包装线上，贴标头与检查相机相隔几个箱位。乔薇第一次右调后，下一张画面仍来自调整前已经贴好的纸箱，她又右调一次；等两次调整对应的纸箱陆续到达相机，标签从接近中央变成偏右。她随后给调整后的第一只纸箱贴黄点，等它到达相机再决定下一步。
storyParagraphs: Before the afternoon truck is loaded, Qiao Wei notices that the shipping labels on the gift boxes are clearly too far left, already close to the fold in the box face. The scanner can still read them now, but if they move any farther, the label edge may lift near the fold. She needs to bring the position back into an acceptable range before this batch goes onto the truck, while the conveyor keeps feeding boxes.

Qiao Wei moves the labeling head slightly to the right. The next camera image still shows the label too far left, so she moves it slightly to the right again. She glances at the loading clock, her hand still on the knob; the same fold is beside the label on the screen. But several box positions separate the labeling head from the inspection camera, and the boxes currently appearing on the screen were labeled earlier, before her first adjustment.

The first boxes actually affected by the first adjustment finally reach the camera, and their labels are already close to the center. Immediately afterward, boxes affected by the second adjustment arrive, and the labels continue moving right, past the position she wanted. Qiao Wei now matches the two actions with the two groups of boxes: when she made the second correction, she had not yet seen the result of the first.

She pulls the clearly misplaced boxes aside for relabeling without stopping the line. To bring the rightward error back toward the center, she makes one adjustment to the left, then sticks a removable yellow dot beside the label on the first box affected. The next boxes keep moving; she cannot yet know whether this change is enough. Only when the yellow dot enters the camera view does she use that box’s label to decide her next step.

By the time the yellow dot appears on the screen, a few more boxes are waiting beside her for new labels. The loader asks how much longer she needs. Qiao Wei asks him to take the row already checked while she relabels the boxes that are clearly off-center. The last rows are now within the acceptable range. She pushes the relabeled boxes back into the queue and peels off the final yellow dot.
storyParagraphsZh: 下午装车前，乔薇发现礼盒上的物流标签明显偏左，已经靠近箱面的折线。扫码枪现在还能读，但再偏一点，标签边缘就可能翘起来。她得在这批箱子上车前把位置拉回去，而输送带还在继续送盒子。
乔薇把贴标头往右调了一点。下一张相机画面里，标签还是偏左，她于是又往右调了一点。她看了一眼出货钟，手还没离开旋钮：屏幕上仍是左边那道折线。可贴标头和检查相机之间隔着几个箱位，此刻相机看到的纸箱，都是更早以前已经贴完标签的。
第一批真正受第一次调整影响的箱子终于走到相机前，标签已经接近中央。紧接着，受第二次调整影响的箱子到了，标签又继续往右，越过了她想要的位置。乔薇这才把两次动作和两批箱子对应起来：第二次修正发生时，她其实还没有看到第一次修正的结果。
她把几只偏得明显的箱子拉到旁边准备重贴，没有停掉整条线。要把偏右的位置拉回来，她这次只向左调一次，然后在调整后贴出的第一只纸箱的标签旁贴一枚可撕的小黄点。接下来几只箱子仍会继续往前，她还不能立刻知道这一调够不够。等黄点真正进入相机画面，她才根据那只箱子的标签决定下一步。
等黄点出现在屏幕上，旁边已经多了几只待重贴的箱子。装车的人来问还有多久，乔薇请他先推走已经检查好的那一排，自己把偏得明显的标签重新贴正。最后几排箱子都回到可接受的位置。她把重贴好的箱子推回队伍，顺手撕掉最后一枚小黄点。
explanationParagraphs: Feedback control adjusts an input according to the measured difference between the result and the target, but the controlled process and measurement path can include response or transport delay. The feedback visible now may therefore correspond to an earlier action.

For example, if the camera is three box positions downstream from the labeling head, the first box affected by an adjustment has not yet reached the camera while the next images may still show the old setting. Repeating the same-direction adjustment too early can therefore accumulate into overshoot.
explanationParagraphsZh: 反馈控制根据测得结果与目标的偏差调整输入，但被控对象和测量常有响应或传输延迟；因此当前看到的反馈可能对应较早的动作。
例如相机位于贴标头下游3个箱位时，一次调整后的第一只箱子尚未到相机前，接下来的画面仍可能来自旧设置；过早再次同向调整就可能叠加过头。
articles.overallZh: 本篇讲反馈控制中的一个简单动态问题：测量结果可能滞后于刚刚做出的调节。如果在前一次作用尚未反映到测量位置前，就依据旧反馈继续同方向修正，多个动作会叠加并造成过调。本篇只说明这种延迟入口，不讨论完整控制器设计。

第二次调整对应的箱子随后到达，标签继续向右并出现过调

先到的箱子接近中心，后到的箱子偏右，使两次调整的效果可以区分。

两次右调 → 在旧反馈下叠加的控制动作。
标签旁的小黄点 → 把一次调整与其后续测量结果对应起来的物件。
moduleZh.boundary: 测量和动作之间有延迟时，尚未显现的前一次纠正可能被下一次叠加。本篇只展示这种过调，不把“小调＋等待”当成普遍最佳方案。合适幅度和等待取决于对象、输送速度、箱距及测量位置；判断未得到新画面前，产线可能仍做出需要重贴的箱子。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果相机被移到贴标头旁边，调整后的箱子几乎立刻就能被看到，乔薇为什么不必继续照搬原来的等待长度？

articles.overall: This article introduces one dynamic issue in feedback control: the measured result can lag behind a recent adjustment. If another correction in the same direction is made before the effect of the previous action has reached the measurement point, the actions can accumulate and cause overshoot. The article focuses only on this delay mechanism and does not teach complete controller design.

module.intro: Follow a box from the labeling head to the camera, distinguishing the image being seen now from the most recent adjustment.
module.diagramTitle: Which Adjustment Does This Image Show?

The next camera image still comes from a box labeled before the adjustment, so she makes a second rightward adjustment
When the boxes corresponding to the first adjustment reach the camera, their labels are already near the center
Boxes corresponding to the second adjustment arrive next and continue moving right, creating overshoot
For later adjustments, mark the first affected box with a yellow dot and wait for its camera result before deciding the next action

While the screen still shows a leftward error, the first adjustment has not yet reached the measurement point.
Earlier boxes are near the center and later ones are too far right, making the two effects distinguishable.
The dot sits beside the label and travels into the same camera view.
The line keeps running, so boxes needing relabeling may still appear while she waits. A correction needs its corresponding observation; waiting does not necessarily create rejects.
mapping: Shipping label too far left → the visible output that needs correction.
Downstream camera → the measurement point with transport delay.
Two rightward adjustments → control actions accumulated while viewing old feedback.
Yellow dot beside the label → a physical marker linking one adjustment to its later measured result.
module.boundary: With delay between action and measurement, a correction whose effect is still unseen may be compounded by the next action. This example shows that overshoot, without claiming “small adjustment plus waiting” is universally best. The appropriate size and interval depend on the process, conveyor speed, spacing, and measurement point. Until a new image confirms the change, the running line may still make boxes that need relabeling.
module.reflection: If the camera were moved next to the labeling head so that an adjusted box could be seen almost immediately, why would Qiao Wei no longer need to copy the original waiting interval?

references.use: Supports dynamic response and delay in feedback systems, closed-loop correction, and the possibility that overly strong or premature corrections can produce oscillation or overshoot.

articles.title: Louder Headphones, the Same Lost Words
articles.titleZh: 耳机更响，句尾还是听不清
articles.summary: A pottery studio needs to finish recording an interview before closing, while the ventilation equipment cannot be turned off. A Lan first increases the recording input gain on the same microphone; the voice and fan noise both become louder, without becoming noticeably easier to distinguish. She then moves the microphone closer to the craftsperson so that the target voice is relatively stronger before entering the recorder, and sets an appropriate input gain before completing the recording.
articles.summaryZh: 陶艺馆要在闭馆前录好一段访谈，抽风设备不能停。阿岚先提高同一支麦克风的录音输入增益，人声和风扇声一起变大，却没有明显更容易辨认。她把麦克风移近师傅，让目标人声在进入录音设备之前相对更强，再重新设好输入增益完成录音。
storyParagraphs: Only half an hour remains before the community pottery studio closes. A Lan needs to finish a three-minute interview with the craftsperson for the course page the next day. The ventilation equipment beside the kiln room is still running and cannot simply be shut down for the recording. She puts on the headphones. The craftsperson's voice is audible, but the steady fan noise lies underneath every sentence, especially covering the ends of phrases.

A Lan first raises the input gain—the setting that amplifies sound entering the recorder. The craftsperson immediately sounds louder in the headphones, but the fan noise also grows louder, and even small taps of tools against the table become more noticeable. She asks the craftsperson to repeat the opening sentence. The overall level is higher, but the words are not noticeably easier to distinguish. She returns the input gain to an appropriate range and tries a different approach.

She moves the same microphone from the middle of the table closer to the craftsperson’s mouth, leaving the ventilation in place. She asks for the same sentence at the same speaking volume. This time she can hear the ending that was blurred before. As she listens, A Lan adjusts the recording level, leaving room for louder speech without exceeding the recorder’s range. Before filming, she records ten seconds for the craftsperson to hear.

The craftsperson nods after listening. A Lan checks the picture: the microphone now takes up a large patch beside the cup. “At least we’ve got a clear shot of that.” Reaching for the cup moves the speaker away from the microphone again. They shift the stool half a step so the cup is within reach and the speaking position stays steady. Some equipment remains in the frame; A Lan leaves it there instead of returning it to the middle of the table.

After the final take, the craftsperson puts the cup back on the table. A Lan stops recording, adjusts only the headphone playback volume to a comfortable level, and listens to the opening again. The sentence “This cup took longer than I expected” is already stored in the recording. Fan noise is still present underneath it, but the words are much easier to distinguish than they were at the start.
storyParagraphsZh: 社区陶艺馆闭馆前只剩半小时，阿岚要录完一段三分钟的师傅访谈，第二天放到课程页面。窑房旁的抽风设备还在运行，不能为了录音随便停。她戴上耳机，师傅的声音能听见，可持续的风扇底声铺在每句话下面，句尾尤其容易被盖住。
阿岚先把输入增益调高，也就是把进入录音机的声音放大。耳机里师傅马上更响，风扇声也一起更响，连桌面轻碰工具的声音都更明显。她让师傅把开头那句话再说一遍，整体音量变大了，字却没有因此明显更容易分辨。她把输入增益退回合适范围，开始换另一个办法。
她把同一支麦克风从桌子中央移到离师傅嘴边更近的位置，抽风设备仍在原处。她请师傅用刚才的音量重说同一句，这回先前含混的句尾听见了。阿岚边听边调好录音音量，免得师傅说话稍大声就超出设备范围。正式开拍前，她录了十秒给师傅听。
师傅听完点头，阿岚看了一眼画面，麦克风却占了杯子旁的一大块。“这回倒是把它拍清楚了。”师傅伸手拿杯子，人又离话筒远了。两个人把凳子挪了半步，让杯子够得到，讲话位置也稳住。镜头里仍露着一点设备，阿岚没有再把它挪回桌子中央。
最后一遍录完，师傅把杯子放回桌上。阿岚停止录音，把耳机的回放音量调到舒服的位置，再听开头。那句“这只杯子，做得比我想的慢”已经保存在录音里，声音仍伴着风扇底声，却比最初容易辨认得多。
explanationParagraphs: Signal-to-noise ratio compares target-signal power with noise power. At the same measurement point and bandwidth, a higher ratio usually means the target is more prominent relative to the background, although intelligibility also depends on spectrum and other factors.

Using relative power units under the same measurement conditions, let signal S = 4 and noise N = 1, so S/N = 4. Ideal linear gain that doubles both amplitudes multiplies both powers by four: 16/4 is still 4. Common amplification does not improve the ratio. If moving the microphone increases voice power while noise remains approximately unchanged, the ratio increases.
explanationParagraphsZh: 信噪比比较目标信号功率与噪声功率。在相同测量位置和带宽下，比例越高通常表示目标相对背景更突出，但“可懂度”还会受频谱和其他因素影响。
取同一测量条件下的相对功率单位：信号S＝4、噪声N＝1，则S/N＝4。理想线性增益让两者幅度都翻倍时，功率各变为四倍，16/4仍为4；只共同放大不会改善比值。若移动麦克风只让人声功率增大而噪声近似不变，比值才会提高。
articles.overallZh: 本篇讲信噪比的直觉入口：目标信号是否容易从背景中分辨，关键在信号与噪声的相对大小，而不只是总音量。理想线性增益若把已有信号和噪声等比例放大，不会改善原有信噪比；本故事通过让麦克风更靠近人声，使进入设备前的目标信号相对增强。

moduleZh.intro: 把“更响”和“目标相对背景更突出”分开：先看共同放大为什么没有帮助，再看输入端相对关系怎样改变。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 音量变大，为什么句尾仍不清楚？
diagramSteps: 同一麦克风同时收到师傅人声和持续风扇背景
提高录音输入增益后，两者一起变响，但辨认没有明显改善
把同一麦克风移近师傅，使进入设备前的人声相对更强
正式录音前重新设置输入增益并留出余量
录完后只调整耳机回放音量，保存下来的录音内容不再改变
diagramStepNotes: 人声与风扇声由同一支麦克风接收，输入增益共同作用于它们。
理想等比例线性放大不会改变已有信号与噪声的功率比。
靠近人声改善的是进入录音设备前的相对水平。
真实放大器还可能增加自身噪声或出现饱和，因此不一定像理想模型。
回放音量属于听取保存文件的设置，不是录音输入增益。
mapping: 持续抽风声 → 稳定背景噪声。
录音输入增益旋钮 → 同时作用于进入设备的已有信号与噪声。
移近的麦克风 → 提高目标人声相对输入水平的动作。
进入画面的麦克风 → 改善相对信号所付出的具体拍摄代价。
moduleZh.boundary: SNR比较需要明确相同测量点、带宽和统计条件；真实噪声可能随频率和时间变化，放大器也可能增加噪声或失真。较高SNR通常有利于分辨目标，但不与所有语音可懂度情形一一等同。滤波和平均也有带宽、瞬态和噪声统计等限制，本篇不展开。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果已经录好的文件里人声和风扇声都偏小，只把播放器回放音量提高两倍，为什么人声通常不会因此相对风扇变得更突出？

referencesZh.citation: National Instruments. Engineer’s Guide to the Digitization of Analog Signals, pp. 34–38.
referencesZh.use: 支持信噪比以平均信号/噪声功率或RMS幅度关系表示，并支持理解滤波、平均及其带宽和噪声统计限制。

articles.overall: This article introduces the intuition behind signal-to-noise ratio: how easily a target signal stands out from the background depends on the relative levels of signal and noise, not merely on total loudness. If ideal linear gain amplifies an existing signal and noise proportionally, it does not improve the original SNR. In the story, moving the microphone closer to the voice makes the target signal relatively stronger before it enters the recording device.

module.intro: Separate “louder” from “more prominent relative to the background”: first see why common amplification does not help, then see how the input relationship changes before recording.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does a Louder Recording Still Lose the Words?
diagramSteps: The same microphone receives both the craftsperson's voice and the steady fan background
Increasing recording input gain makes both louder, without noticeably improving distinction
Move the same microphone closer to the craftsperson so the voice is relatively stronger before entering the device
Reset the input gain before the formal recording and leave enough headroom
After recording, adjust only headphone playback volume; the saved recording itself no longer changes
diagramStepNotes: The voice and fan are received by the same microphone; input gain acts on both.
Ideal proportional linear amplification does not change the existing signal-to-noise power ratio.
Moving closer to the speaker improves the relative input level of the target voice in this scenario.
A real amplifier may also add its own noise or saturate, so real behavior need not match the ideal model exactly.
Playback volume is a setting for listening to the saved file, not recording input gain.
mapping: Continuous ventilation noise → the stable background noise.
Recording input-gain control → a control that raises the existing signal and noise entering the device.
Microphone moved closer → an action that makes the target voice relatively stronger at the input.
Microphone visible in the frame → the concrete filming cost of improving the relative signal.
module.boundary: SNR comparisons require a defined measurement point, bandwidth, and statistical conditions. Real noise can vary with frequency and time, and amplifiers can add noise or distortion. Higher SNR usually helps distinguish a target but is not identical to speech intelligibility in every situation. Filtering and averaging also involve bandwidth, transient preservation, and noise-statistics trade-offs that this article does not cover.
module.reflection: If the voice and fan are both quiet in an already recorded file, why does doubling only the player's playback volume usually fail to make the voice stand out more relative to the fan?

references.citation: National Instruments. Engineer’s Guide to the Digitization of Analog Signals, pp. 34–38.
references.use: Supports expressing signal-to-noise ratio through average signal/noise power or RMS-amplitude relationships, and supports the limits and trade-offs associated with filtering, averaging, bandwidth, and noise statistics.

articles.summaryZh: 科普馆要演示一个自动注水装置。罗文切断控制电源，运行灯灭了，透明杯里的水却还在流；他得找到真正让水停下来的方式。
storyParagraphsZh: 科普馆准备一个桌面清水演示：按下按钮后，高处的小水箱靠重力把水送过阀门，流进透明杯。第一版通电时，执行机构打开阀门。罗文要验证一个具体情形：如果控制盒突然失去供电，这套演示能不能停止继续往杯里加水？
第一版运行时绿色灯亮着，水稳定流进杯里。罗文切断控制盒电源，灯灭了，可高位水箱仍提供重力压头，水位继续上涨。他从灯旁转向阀门：执行件失去驱动后仍停在开启位置。他先关上水箱另设的手动总阀，结束这一轮。
下一版在阀门上加入预置回位机构：正常时通电保持开启；失电时，回位动作不依赖失去的电源，把阀门推向这次演示选定的关闭位置。检查水箱仍有足够水后，罗文恢复控制盒供电，打开手动总阀并按运行键，让阀门开启、水重新流起来，然后再次切断控制电源。
阀门回到关闭位置后，罗文等管路里可能剩下的水流尽，再确认杯中不再进水。他保持装置停止并检查，再由讲解员按这次演示规程重新启动。这样会中断展示几分钟，也多一道人工确认；这一次，他们看到的不只是灯的变化，还有阀位回转和水流停止。
开放前最后一次排练，讲解员让水流起来，再切断控制盒电源。绿色运行灯灭了，阀门回位，透明杯的水面停止上涨。罗文等了一会儿，确认没有继续流入后，把杯里的水倒进回收桶，再放回托盘。下一场正式演示前，系统仍要按他们约定的步骤重新检查和启动。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用低风险清水演示说明故障安全设计的一个入口：针对明确识别的故障和危险，需要先选定较低风险状态，并让系统在该故障发生时能够实际向这个状态移动。报警或运行指示变化本身不等于执行安全动作；最终还要确认执行件位置和过程结果。
explanationParagraphsZh: 高位水箱的重力供水独立于控制盒电源。第一版通电时执行机构打开阀门，失去驱动后却可能停在开启位置；新版则在正常运行时用电保持开启，并在失电时由预置机构回位。针对控制供电丢失这一已识别故障，演示把关闭阀门选为较低风险状态。
核对时不能只看指示灯：切断控制供电后，先观察阀门是否实际移到关闭位置，再等可能的下游余水流尽，确认不再进水。灯不亮本身也不能排除灯具或线路故障。一次演示只覆盖这次失电情况，不能证明阀门卡滞、回位机构损坏或其他失效都已控制。

moduleZh.intro: 先定义本场景在失电时希望系统到达的状态，再区分‘知道失电了’和‘执行件真的完成保护动作’。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么运行灯熄灭，还不能证明水已经停了
diagramSteps: 第一版通电时由执行机构打开阀门，高位水箱靠重力供水
切断第一版控制电源：运行灯熄灭，执行件仍停在开启位置
水仍流入杯中；关闭另设的手动总阀结束这一轮
新版通电保持阀门开启；失电后由预置回位机构推动关闭
确认阀位，等下游余水流尽并确认停止，再按演示规程检查重启
diagramStepNotes: 高位水箱的重力供水独立于控制盒电源；第一版未说明有失电回位。
绿色灯是运行指示，灯不亮本身不能排除灯具或线路故障，也不能证明阀位。
另设手动总阀只用来结束这一轮，并不替代新版对失电的自动回位动作。
关闭仅是此清水演示针对控制失电选择的较低风险状态，不是所有过程的通用安全状态。
一次测试只覆盖这一失电情形；卡滞或回位机构损坏需另行分析，人工重启是本例规程。
mapping: 高位小水箱 → 与控制电源独立的重力供水来源。
绿色运行灯 → 正常供电状态的显示，而不是保护动作本身。
失电回位机构 → 在指定失电情形下推动阀门向关闭位置移动的机制。
透明杯水面停止上涨 → 实际过程结果已随阀位改变的可见证据。
moduleZh.boundary: 所谓较低风险状态取决于具体过程与故障。某些真实系统在失电后仍需持续冷却、搅拌、抑制剂供应或其他主动功能，因此‘断电、关闭或停止’并非普遍安全答案。本故事只讨论一个低风险清水注杯演示中的控制供电丢失；不能据此提供真实设备改装、测试、认证或风险分析方法。保护动作也不意味着服务不中断，恢复供电后不一定应自动重启。
moduleZh.reflection: 这次断电试验成功后，若回位机构本身卡住，能否仅凭这一次结果断定阀门仍会关闭？还需另行考虑什么故障？

referencesZh.citation: Health and Safety Executive. Control systems. Technical Measure Document, COMAH Safety Report Assessment Manual.
referencesZh.use: 支持安全功能针对特定危险寻求定义好的安全状态，并支持失去信号或动力时由弹簧回位执行机构进入预定跳闸状态的原则；同时支持考虑公用工程依赖和保护系统测试。该资料也说明某些过程需要持续冷却等功能，因此关闭或断电并非通用安全状态。

referencesZh.citation: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. REGDOC-2.5.2: Design of Reactor Facilities, Version 2.1, section 5.6.6, Fail-safe design.
referencesZh.use: 支持在适用情况下，故障安全设计应考虑部件或系统失效时无需额外操作即可趋向指定安全状态，并考虑失效模式和可检测故障；本篇只借用这一一般原则解释清水教学演示，不把核设施要求当成其他设备的设计认证。

articles.title: After the Running Light Went Dark
articles.summary: A science museum is preparing an automatic water-filling demonstration. Luo Wen cuts the control power and the running light goes dark, but water still enters the clear cup. He needs a way to make it stop.
storyParagraphs: The science museum is preparing a tabletop water demonstration. When a button is pressed, a small elevated tank sends water by gravity through a valve and into a clear cup. In the first version, the powered actuator opens the valve. Luo Wen wants to check one situation: if the control box suddenly loses power, can the demonstration stop adding water to the cup?

In the first version, the green running light is on and water flows steadily into the cup. Luo Wen cuts power to the control box. The light goes out, but the elevated tank still provides gravitational head and the level continues to rise. He turns from the lamp to the valve: the actuator has lost its drive yet remains in its open position, leaving the valve open. He closes a separate manual tank shutoff to end the first trial.

The next version adds a preset return mechanism: power holds the valve open during normal operation; on power loss, the return action uses no lost electrical supply and moves the valve toward the closed position selected for this demonstration. After checking that the tank still contains enough water, Luo Wen restores control power, opens the manual tank shutoff and presses the run button. With the valve open and water flowing again, he cuts control power once more.

After the valve returns to the closed position, Luo Wen waits for any water remaining downstream to drain, then confirms that no more enters the cup. He keeps the apparatus stopped and checks it before the presenter restarts it under this demonstration’s procedure. That interrupts the display for several minutes and adds a manual check. This time they have observed more than a change in the light: the valve moved and the water stopped.

During the final rehearsal before opening, the presenter starts the water and then cuts power to the control box. The green running light goes out, the valve returns, and the water level in the clear cup stops rising. Luo Wen waits for a moment to confirm that no more water is entering, pours the cup into the recovery container, and puts it back on the tray. Before the next public demonstration, the system will still be checked and restarted according to their agreed procedure.
articles.overall: This article uses a low-risk water demonstration to introduce one aspect of fail-safe design: for a specifically identified failure and hazard, a lower-risk state must first be selected, and the system should actually move toward that state when the failure occurs. An alarm or change in operating indication is not itself the protective action; the actuator position and the resulting process state also need to be verified.
explanationParagraphs: The elevated tank’s gravity-driven water supply is independent of the control-box power. In the first version, the powered actuator opens the valve but may remain open after losing drive. In the new version, power holds it open during normal operation and a preset mechanism returns it on power loss. For the identified control-power failure, the demonstration selects valve closure as the lower-risk state.

The check cannot rely on the indicator light alone. After control power is cut, observe whether the valve actually moves closed, then allow any downstream residual water to drain and confirm that inflow stops. A dark light alone cannot rule out a failed bulb or wiring. One demonstration covers only this power-loss case; it does not prove that valve sticking, return-mechanism damage or other faults have been controlled.

module.intro: First define the state this scenario should reach after loss of power, then separate 'knowing that power is gone' from 'the actuator actually completing the protective action.'
module.diagramTitle: Why Doesn't the Running Light Going Out Prove That the Water Has Stopped?
diagramSteps: In the first powered version, the actuator opens the valve and the elevated tank supplies water by gravity
Cut first-version control power: the running light goes dark while the actuator remains in its open position, leaving the valve open
Water continues into the cup; close the separate manual tank shutoff to end the trial
In the new version, power holds the valve open; loss of power triggers the preset return toward closed
Check the valve, let downstream residual water drain and confirm flow stops, then check and restart under the demonstration procedure
diagramStepNotes: The elevated tank supplies water by gravity independently of the control box; the first version has no specified loss-of-power return.
The green lamp is a running indicator. Darkness alone cannot rule out bulb or wiring failure and does not prove valve position.
The separate manual shutoff ends this trial; it is not a substitute for the new version’s automatic return on loss of power.
Closure is the lower-risk state selected for this water demonstration and control-power failure, not a universal safe state.
One test covers only this power-loss case; sticking or return-mechanism damage needs separate analysis, and manual restart is this demonstration’s procedure.
mapping: Elevated small water tank → the gravity-driven water source independent of control power.
Green running light → indication of normal powered operation, not the protective action itself.
Loss-of-power return mechanism → the mechanism that moves the valve toward the closed position for the specified failure.
Water level in the clear cup stops rising → visible evidence that the process result has changed with the valve position.
module.boundary: The lower-risk state depends on the specific process and failure. Some real systems still require active cooling, mixing, inhibitor addition, or other functions after loss of power, so 'power off, close, or stop' is not a universal safe answer. It does not provide a method for modifying, testing, certifying, or performing risk analysis on real equipment. A protective action also does not mean service remains uninterrupted, and restoration of power does not necessarily justify automatic restart.

articles.summaryZh: 第二批试条比旧批多拉长了一倍，退货单已经打印。顾岚却在两张测试单上看见了不同的原长、截面积和拉力。
storyParagraphsZh: 下午四点前，金属工作室要回复供应商：第二批薄拉带到底收下，还是让来取货的司机原车带回去。顾岚桌上摊着两张测试单，新批那张写着“伸长0.2 mm”，旧批只有0.1 mm。同事已经把退货单打印出来一半——如果新材料真的更容易被拉长，后面的下料就得停。

平时工作室拿到的是相同尺寸的试样，直接比较伸长多少毫米很方便。这次实验室用了两条大小不同的直试条。每条都沿长度方向受拉，两道标记之间那一段粗细均匀，记录的原长就是两道标记的初始距离。旧批原长100 mm、原截面积10 mm²，在100 N拉力下伸长0.1 mm；新批原长200 mm、原截面积20 mm²，在200 N下伸长0.2 mm。顾岚把两条记录并排放好，第二条两道标记之间的原长，是第一条的两倍。
她没有继续只盯着0.1和0.2。旧批的100 N分到原来的10 mm²上，是10 MPa；新批200 N分到原来的20 mm²上，也是10 MPa。再看伸长占原长的比例：0.1/100=0.001，0.2/200也等于0.001。原来看起来翻倍的伸长，在把原始尺寸一起算进去后，这一个测试点并没有拉开差别。
顾岚把退货单从打印机旁拿回来，却没有在新批上盖“没问题”。这一点的结果相同，还不能回答更大载荷下会怎样。她让第二批留在待检架上，要求后续用可比尺寸的试样继续测试，下料因此推迟了半天。
供应商司机到门口时问：“这箱还带走吗？”顾岚把封箱胶带放回桌上：“先留着，别急着退。”那张写着0.2 mm的测试单仍压在箱子上，旁边多了一行手写字：原长200 mm。
articles.overallZh: 比较两条不同尺寸的试样时，拉力要结合原截面积，伸长要结合原长。把记录换成这两个比值，才能比较故事中的同一个测试点；结果相同并不证明两批材料的强度或断裂表现也相同。
explanationParagraphsZh: 工程应力在这个简单轴向拉伸例子中写作F/A0，其中A0是测试前的原截面积；工程应变写作ΔL/L0，其中L0是原标距长度。这两个比值让力和伸长都按试样测试前的尺寸来比较。
最小例子：100 N作用在原截面积10 mm²上，工程应力为10 N/mm²=10 MPa；原长100 mm、伸长0.1 mm，工程应变为0.1/100=0.001=0.1%。这些只是教学数字，不是现实选材或安全参数。

moduleZh.intro: 先看为什么“多伸了多少毫米”可能被试样尺寸误导，再把力和伸长分别除以对应的初始几何量。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 同样的相对受力与变形，为什么原始毫米数可以不同
diagramSteps: 旧批试样原长100 mm、原截面积10 mm²，在100 N下伸长0.1 mm
新批试样原长200 mm、原截面积20 mm²，在200 N下伸长0.2 mm
用测试前原截面积计算，两者工程应力都是10 MPa
用原长计算，两者工程应变都是0.001
因此这个测试点不能仅凭0.2 mm大于0.1 mm判定第二批材料更差
diagramStepNotes: 先保留旧批试样测试前的尺寸、拉力和伸长记录。
新批也保留同样几类记录，不单凭伸长毫米数比较。
一个测试点相同，不代表完整曲线、屈服或断裂表现相同。
mapping: 0.1 mm与0.2 mm → 尚未按原长归一化的绝对伸长。
10 mm²与20 mm² → 计算本例工程应力时使用的原截面积。
10 MPa与0.001 → 两条试样在这个教学测试点上的归一化比较结果。
暂缓的退货单 → 重新理解测量记录后改变的决定。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只处理均匀标距段、轴向拉伸下的工程应力F/A0和工程应变ΔL/L0，并用小变形教学数字说明几何归一化。它不提供完整应力—应变曲线，也不能由一个点推断屈服、强度、断裂、疲劳、结构安全或现实选材结论。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果一条原长200 mm的试样伸长0.2 mm，另一条原长100 mm的试样伸长0.15 mm，哪一条相对原长的变形更大？

referencesZh.citation: Roylance, D. (2001, August 23). Stress-Strain Curves. Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Department of Materials Science and Engineering.
referencesZh.use: 支持工程应力使用原截面积、工程应变使用原长度，以及初始弹性响应与永久变形属于不同判断；本篇只取其入门定义，不用于结构选材或安全认证。

articles.title: Hold That Box of Metal Strips
articles.summary: The new-batch specimen stretches twice as far, and the return form is already being printed. But Gu Lan notices that the two test sheets also list different original lengths, cross-sectional areas, and forces.
storyParagraphs: Before 16:00, the metalworking shop has to tell the supplier whether to keep the second batch of thin metal strips or send it back on the same truck that is coming for collection. Two test sheets are spread across Gu Lan's desk. The new-batch sheet says “elongation 0.2 mm,” while the old batch shows only 0.1 mm. A colleague has already printed half of the return form—if the new material really does stretch more easily, the downstream cutting work has to stop.

Normally, the shop receives specimens of the same dimensions, so comparing their elongation in millimeters is convenient. This time the lab used two straight specimens of different sizes. Each was pulled along its length, and the section between two marks had a uniform cross-section; the recorded original length was the initial distance between those marks. The old-batch specimen started at 100 mm with an original cross-sectional area of 10 mm² and elongated 0.1 mm under 100 N. The new-batch specimen started at 200 mm with an original cross-sectional area of 20 mm² and elongated 0.2 mm under 200 N. Gu Lan places the two records side by side. The original distance between the marks on the second specimen was twice that on the first.

She stops looking only at 0.1 and 0.2. For the old batch, 100 N divided by the original 10 mm² gives 10 MPa; for the new batch, 200 N divided by the original 20 mm² also gives 10 MPa. Then she compares elongation with original length: 0.1/100=0.001, and 0.2/200 also equals 0.001. Once the initial dimensions are included, the apparently doubled elongation does not separate the two records at this test point.

Gu Lan takes the return form back from beside the printer, but she does not stamp the new batch “no problem.” Matching at this point still does not tell her what happens at higher loads. She leaves the second batch on the inspection rack and requests further tests using specimens with comparable dimensions, delaying cutting by half a day.

When the supplier's driver reaches the door, he asks, “Is this box coming back with me?” Gu Lan puts the packing tape back on the table. “Leave it here for now. Don't send it back yet.” The test sheet marked 0.2 mm still lies on top of the box, with one handwritten line added beside it: original length 200 mm.
articles.overall: When comparing two specimens of different sizes, force must be considered alongside original cross-sectional area, and elongation alongside original length. These two ratios make the story’s test point comparable; matching there does not establish matching strength or fracture behavior.
explanationParagraphs: In this simple axial-tension example, engineering stress is written as F/A0, where A0 is the original cross-sectional area before testing. Engineering strain is written as ΔL/L0, where L0 is the original gauge length. These ratios compare force and elongation in relation to the specimen’s dimensions before testing.

Minimal example: 100 N acting on an original cross-sectional area of 10 mm² gives an engineering stress of 10 N/mm²=10 MPa. With an original length of 100 mm and an elongation of 0.1 mm, engineering strain is 0.1/100=0.001=0.1%. These are teaching values, not real-world material-selection or safety parameters.

module.intro: First see why “how many millimeters longer” can be misleading when specimen size changes, then divide force and elongation by the corresponding original geometric quantities.
module.diagramTitle: Why Raw Elongation Can Differ Even When Relative Loading and Deformation Are the Same
diagramSteps: The old-batch specimen starts at 100 mm with an original cross-sectional area of 10 mm² and elongates 0.1 mm under 100 N
The new-batch specimen starts at 200 mm with an original cross-sectional area of 20 mm² and elongates 0.2 mm under 200 N
Using the original cross-sectional areas, both engineering stresses are 10 MPa
Using the original lengths, both engineering strains are 0.001
Therefore this test point does not justify calling the second batch worse merely because 0.2 mm is greater than 0.1 mm
diagramStepNotes: Keep the old specimen’s dimensions before testing, force, and elongation together.
Keep the same kinds of records for the new specimen rather than comparing elongation alone.
100/10=200/20=10 N/mm², giving 10 MPa in both cases.
0.1/100=0.2/200=0.001, or 0.1% of original length.
Matching at one point does not establish matching complete curves, yielding, or fracture behavior.
mapping: 0.1 mm and 0.2 mm → absolute elongations not yet normalized by original length.
10 mm² and 20 mm² → original cross-sectional areas used to calculate engineering stress in this example.
10 MPa and 0.001 → normalized comparison values for the two specimens at this teaching test point.
Return form put on hold → a decision changed after the measurements were reinterpreted.
module.boundary: This article covers only engineering stress F/A0 and engineering strain ΔL/L0 for axial tension in a uniform gauge section, using small-deformation teaching values to illustrate geometric normalization. It does not provide a complete stress-strain curve, and one point cannot be used to infer yield, strength, fracture, fatigue, structural safety, or real-world material-selection conclusions.
module.reflection: If a specimen with an original length of 200 mm elongates by 0.2 mm while a specimen with an original length of 100 mm elongates by 0.15 mm, which one changes more relative to its original length?

references.citation: Roylance, D. (2001, August 23). Stress-Strain Curves. Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Department of Materials Science and Engineering.
references.use: Supports the use of original cross-sectional area for engineering stress, original length for engineering strain, and the distinction between initial elastic response and permanent deformation. This article uses only the introductory definitions and does not use the source for structural selection or safety certification.

articles.summaryZh: 产品实验室要决定下一版展示架是否继续使用一枚小金属弹片。一次加载检查原本通过就能推进，乔宁却想知道，反复开合会留下什么。
storyParagraphsZh: 产品实验室正在改一款折叠展示架，里面有一枚小金属弹片，每次展开和收起都会经历一次加载变化。乔宁要决定下一轮样件是否继续沿用这个结构。团队原本准备只做一次峰值加载检查：如果试片承受设定峰值力后卸载，表面检查没有新发现，就继续推进下一版。
乔宁却把真实使用动作又想了一遍：展示架不会只开合一次。她从同一批材料里准备两枚同材质、名义几何相同的独立试片，测试前用同一方法检查关注区域的表面，两枚都没有记录到可见裂纹。
两枚试片在同一台仪器和同样环境中，使用同一工装、加载方向和设定峰值力。第一枚只完成一次从低载荷升到峰值力再卸载的过程，随后被取下。第二枚留在仪器上，反复经历同样的加载—卸载循环。乔宁把两片的测试记录放在一起，等着下一次检查。
第一枚单次加载后，用同一检查方法仍没有记录到新的可见表面裂纹。第二枚在循环初期也没有新发现。实验人员按既定间隔暂停循环，用同样方法观察同一关注区域；经过一段循环历史后，发现了一条此前没有记录到的细裂纹，后续检查中这条裂纹又比前一次更长了一些。
乔宁把下一轮样机计划往后移了几天，并增加更多同几何试片，用于受控循环加载和后续观察。原定送去装配的下一版弹片因此暂时留在实验室周转架上。负责样机的人来取件时，她没有交出那盒零件：“再等几天。一次加载告诉我们的，还不够回答反复开合。”
articles.overallZh: 本篇用低风险教学试片说明材料疲劳的一个入口：金属在反复变化的载荷下，裂纹可能逐渐萌生并扩展，因此一次峰值加载后没有发现问题，并不能代表相同构件能够承受完整的循环载荷历史。疲劳判断需要关注载荷循环、裂纹发展和相关检查，而不仅是一次峰值。
explanationParagraphsZh: 疲劳与重复或波动载荷有关。在某些金属和条件下，裂纹可以在循环历史中萌生并逐渐扩展，最终导致性能下降甚至断裂。单次加载没有出现可见问题，只说明那一次观察的结果，不能替代对循环历史的判断。
本例的对照让两枚独立试片的批次、名义几何、峰值力、工装、加载方向、仪器和环境尽量可比；一枚只加载一次，另一枚反复循环。循环试片后来首次被记录到细裂纹，后续检查又看到它变长，说明这一加载历史值得继续研究。首次发现不等于证明裂纹当时才萌生；两片试样也不能排除未检微缺陷、材料离散或确定通用寿命。

moduleZh.intro: 让试片批次、名义几何、峰值力、工装方向、仪器和环境尽量可比，再比较一次与反复加载的观察。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么一次峰值加载后未发现可见裂纹，仍不能代表反复开合也没问题
diagramSteps: 准备两枚同批、同材质、名义几何相同的独立试片，并用同一方法做初始表面检查
在同一仪器和环境下，用同一工装、方向、设定峰值力和加载—卸载方式测试两片
第一片只完成一次加载后卸载，随后停止测试
第二片反复循环，并按既定间隔用同一方法检查同一关注区域
若循环试片后来首次被记录到细裂纹且后续观察变长，则下一轮开发增加循环验证
diagramStepNotes: 初始检查没有发现可见裂纹，不代表排除了所有微小缺陷或材料离散。
峰值力、工装、加载方向和方式尽量一致，降低已记录条件差异；未检微缺陷仍可能不同。
单次试片在一次卸载后不再参与循环，因此不会发生时间顺序上的重复加载混淆。
定期检查只能在所用方法的能力范围内观察裂纹，不意味着每个循环都产生可见增长。
一对教学试片不能确定真实构件寿命、唯一根因或所有材料在所有应力水平下的疲劳表现。
mapping: 一次加载试片 → 单次峰值条件下的有限观察。
重复循环试片 → 具有累积加载历史的教学对照。
后来首次被记录且后续变长的细裂纹 → 检出与扩展的观察，不能单凭首次发现确定萌生时间。
推迟下一版样机 → 为加入循环验证付出的开发时间和样件成本。
moduleZh.boundary: 疲劳寿命受应力范围、平均应力、频率、几何、材料、加工、缺陷和环境等影响。早期裂纹可能低于表面检查的检测能力；初始微缺陷、腐蚀、磨损或未记录超载等也可能影响结果。两片教学试样不能确定唯一根因或真实构件寿命。本例没有足够应力资料判断是否屈服，也不提供检修方法、循环次数、载荷阈值或通用疲劳极限。
moduleZh.reflection: 某零件出厂时肉眼没有发现裂纹，使用一段时间后显微检查发现一道细纹。能断定裂纹一定是在使用之后才萌生吗？还需要知道哪些检查条件？

referencesZh.citation: Deschanel, S., Ben Rhouma, W., & Weiss, J. (2017). Acoustic emission multiplets as early warnings of fatigue failure in metallic materials. Scientific Reports, 7, 13680. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-13226-1

referencesZh.citation: Federal Aviation Administration. Technical Discipline: Fatigue and Damage Tolerance. Updated April 9, 2026.
referencesZh.use: 支持疲劳与反复或波动载荷、环境因素、断裂力学和寿命管理有关的广泛范围；该航空资料不用于提供本虚构金属试片的通用检查间隔、寿命或疲劳强度。

articles.title: A Few More Days for the Spring Element
articles.summary: A product laboratory must decide whether its next folding display stand will keep a small metal spring element. A single load check was meant to clear the way, but Qiao Ning wants to know what repeated opening and closing might leave behind.
storyParagraphs: The product laboratory is revising a folding display stand. Inside it is a small metal spring element that experiences a load change each time the stand is opened and closed. Qiao Ning has to decide whether the next prototype should keep this structure. The team had originally planned only a one-time peak-force check: if a specimen was loaded to the specified peak force, unloaded, and showed no newly recorded visible surface crack, they would move on to the next prototype.

Qiao Ning thinks again about how the product is actually used: the stand will not be opened and closed only once. She prepares two independent specimens from the same material batch with the same material and nominal geometry. Before testing, the same method records no visible surface cracks in the area of interest on either specimen.

The two specimens are tested in the same machine and environment with the same fixture, loading direction and specified peak force. The first makes one rise from a low load to that peak and is unloaded, then removed. The second remains in the machine for repeated cycles of the same loading and unloading. Qiao Ning puts the two test records side by side and waits for the next inspection.

After its single loading event, the first specimen is inspected again using the same method, and no newly recorded visible surface crack is found. The cyclic specimen also shows no new finding early in the test. At predetermined intervals, the laboratory pauses the cycling and examines the same region using the same method. After some cyclic history has accumulated, a fine crack that had not previously been recorded is found. In a later inspection, that crack is longer than it was before.

Qiao Ning moves the next prototype schedule back by several days and adds more specimens of the same geometry for controlled cyclic loading and follow-up observation. The next batch of spring elements that had been scheduled for assembly therefore remains on the laboratory transfer rack. When the prototype colleague comes to collect them, she does not hand over the box. “Give me a few more days. One load doesn't tell us enough about repeated opening and closing.”
articles.overall: This article uses low-risk teaching specimens to introduce one aspect of material fatigue: under repeated or fluctuating loading, cracks can initiate and gradually grow, so a specimen showing no problem after a single peak load does not establish its ability to withstand an entire cyclic loading history. Fatigue reasoning therefore requires attention to load cycles, crack development, and relevant inspection rather than only to one peak event.
explanationParagraphs: Fatigue is associated with repeated or fluctuating loads. In some metals and conditions, cracks can initiate during cyclic loading and grow progressively, eventually reducing performance or leading to fracture. A one-time load with no visible problem reports only the result of that particular observation; it cannot replace consideration of cyclic history.

The comparison makes the two independent specimens’ batch, nominal geometry, peak force, fixture, loading direction, machine and environment as comparable as possible. One is loaded once and the other cycled repeatedly. A fine crack is first recorded later in the cyclic specimen and is observed to grow in a subsequent inspection, making that loading history worth further study. First detection does not prove when the crack initiated; two specimens cannot rule out undetected microscopic defects or material variability, or establish a universal life.

module.intro: Make batch, nominal geometry, peak force, fixture and direction, machine and environment as comparable as possible, then compare observations after one versus repeated loading.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does Finding No Visible Crack After One Peak Load Not Prove Repeated Opening and Closing Will Be Fine?
diagramSteps: Prepare two independent specimens from the same batch with the same material and nominal geometry, and inspect both initially using the same surface method
Test both in the same machine and environment, using the same fixture, direction, peak force and loading-unloading pattern
Load the first specimen once to the peak force, unload it, and then remove it from further cyclic testing
Cycle the second specimen repeatedly and inspect the same region at predetermined intervals using the same method
If a previously unrecorded fine crack is later found in the cyclic specimen and observed to grow, add cyclic validation to the next development round
diagramStepNotes: No visible crack recorded during the initial inspection does not mean all microscopic defects or material variability have been excluded.
Match peak force, fixture, direction and loading pattern to reduce known differences; undetected microscopic defects may still differ.
The single-load specimen does not enter the later cyclic sequence, preventing confusion about its time history.
Periodic inspection can observe cracks only within the capability of the chosen method and does not mean every cycle produces visible crack growth.
A pair of teaching specimens cannot establish the fatigue life, unique cause, or cyclic behavior of all real components or all materials.
mapping: Single-load specimen → a limited observation under one peak-force event.
Repeated-cycle specimen → a teaching comparison containing accumulated loading history.
A fine crack first recorded later and then observed to grow → an observation of detection and propagation, not proof of when initiation occurred.
Delayed next prototype → the development-time and specimen cost of adding cyclic validation.
module.boundary: Fatigue life depends on stress range, mean stress, frequency, geometry, material, processing, defects, environment and other factors. Early cracks can be below the detection capability of surface inspection; initial microscopic defects, corrosion, wear or unrecorded overload may also affect results. Two teaching specimens cannot establish a unique cause or a real component’s life. This example lacks enough stress information to determine whether yielding occurred, and it provides no inspection procedure, cycle count, load threshold or universal fatigue limit.
module.reflection: A component leaves the factory with no crack seen by eye. After some use, microscopic inspection finds a fine crack. Does that establish that it must have initiated during use? What inspection conditions would you need to know?

references.citation: Deschanel, S., Ben Rhouma, W., & Weiss, J. (2017). Acoustic emission multiplets as early warnings of fatigue failure in metallic materials. Scientific Reports, 7, 13680. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-13226-1
references.use: Supports the basic mechanism of crack initiation, incremental crack growth, and eventual failure under cyclic fatigue, and supports research into incremental crack propagation in particular metallic specimens. The paper's specific specimen dimensions, cycle counts, loads, and low-cycle experimental conditions are not used as fictional story data or universal safety thresholds.

references.citation: Federal Aviation Administration. Technical Discipline: Fatigue and Damage Tolerance. Updated April 9, 2026.
references.use: Supports the broad scope of fatigue involving repeated or fluctuating loads, environmental factors, fracture mechanics, and life management. This aviation source is not used to provide a universal inspection interval, service life, or fatigue strength for the fictional metal specimens.

articles.titleZh: 两块都合格，合起来却宽了0.1毫米
articles.summaryZh: 三十套灯等着发货，两个各自合格的垫片却在第三个铰链里卡住。林悦先量单件，再量两块合在一起占去的空间。
storyParagraphsZh: 傍晚五点，快递要来取三十套折叠阅读灯。林悦装到第三套时，铰链忽然推不进去。她把两块铝垫片取出来，边缘没有毛刺，卡尺量过也都落在图纸允许的50±0.2 mm范围里。单件都合格，为什么两块放在一起反而卡住了？
上一款灯每个位置只用一块这种垫片，所以只要单件尺寸在范围内，装配通常就不会出问题。新款第一次改成两块并排放进同一条槽里。林悦把刚才那一对重新量了一遍：一块接近50.2 mm，另一块也接近50.2 mm；她又量了槽宽，读数是100.3 mm。
两块单独都没越界，可50.2+50.2=100.4 mm，比槽宽多0.1 mm。她从零件盘里拿了一块49.9 mm的合格垫片，和其中一块50.2 mm搭在一起，总长100.1 mm，这一对实际装入后顺利推进。她把两块的尺寸写在同一行，末尾加上合长，再把这张纸放在原来的单件检验记录旁。
当天还剩二十多套没装，林悦不能假定每一对都会碰巧有合适搭档。仓库里这一批共有八十多块已验收垫片，三十套灯总共需要六十块。她和同事把整盘重新量过、分格摆放，再逐对试装，实际凑出了足够的三十对；那些单独合格、但暂时不好与现有库存配成这一槽位组合的零件被留在盒里。
这办法救了当天的交货，却让原先准备随手拿取的零件变成了先量、再配、再试装，整批多花了四十多分钟。设计人员把100.3 mm槽宽和两件50±0.2 mm的组合记进下一版图纸讨论，没有简单要求所有尺寸都无限收紧。快递到门口时，三十套灯已经合上；检验桌上那两块50.2 mm的垫片仍各自合格，只是被装进同一个小袋，袋上写着“合长100.4 mm”。
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一个理想化的一维装配说明工程公差的入门问题：单个零件都落在各自允许范围内，并不自动保证多个尺寸组合后仍满足装配空间。最坏情况下，各项偏差可以在同一方向叠加；临时选配可以解决特定批次，却不等于实现任意合格件互换。
explanationParagraphsZh: 公差允许实际尺寸在规定范围内变化。当多个尺寸沿同一装配方向相加时，每个零件都合格，组合后的总尺寸仍可能超过功能允许范围。
最小例子：两件各为50±0.2 mm，则单件范围是49.8–50.2 mm，两件合长的理想一维范围是99.6–100.4 mm。若固定槽宽为100.3 mm，最大组合100.4 mm会多出0.1 mm。

moduleZh.intro: 先看为什么两件各自合格仍可能组合失败，再用一个一维极值核对偏差怎样累积。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 每块都合格，为什么两块一起仍可能超过100.3毫米
diagramSteps: 每块垫片允许尺寸为50±0.2 mm，即49.8–50.2 mm
两块沿同一方向并排时，最小理想合长为49.8+49.8=99.6 mm
本篇固定理想槽宽为100.3 mm，因此最大组合超出0.1 mm
当天通过实际量测和逐对试装从库存中选出足够组合，但这不恢复任意互换性
diagramStepNotes: 这个例子只处理一维尺寸相加，不涉及完整几何公差。
100.3 mm在本篇中被当作理想固定槽宽，不讨论槽本身的制造变化。
最坏情况把允许范围的极端值组合在一起，不假设误差会自然抵消。
合长不超过槽宽只是本篇简化装入条件，不能单独保证完整铰链性能。
选配增加测量、分组和试装。已经核对的是选定的配对，改换搭配后仍需检查。
mapping: 两块50.2 mm垫片 → 各自合格但组合达到最大100.4 mm。
100.3 mm固定槽 → 这一维教学例子的功能空间限制。
49.9 mm与50.2 mm配对 → 一个实际合长100.1 mm并成功装入的组合。
分格摆放的库存 → 为当天选配付出的额外工作。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只使用明确的一维尺寸范围和理想固定槽宽，展示最坏情况下尺寸偏差如何累积。真实装配还可能涉及槽本身公差、形位误差、间隙、表面状态和其他功能要求，因此“合长不大于槽宽”不能单独证明铰链整体合格。临时选配也不等于设计上保证任意合格件互换，更不意味着所有公差都应一律收紧。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果两块零件仍各允许50±0.2 mm，但固定槽改成100.5 mm，这个一维最坏组合还能因为长度本身而超过槽宽吗？

referencesZh.citation: Sudarsan, R., Roy, U., Narahari, Y., Sriram, R. D., Lyons, K. W., & Pramanik, N. (2000, May). Information Models for Design Tolerancing: From Conceptual to the Detail Design. NISTIR6524.
referencesZh.use: 支持装配功能会受到多个零件尺寸变化累积影响，以及一维最坏情况分析可通过组合允许范围的极端值检查功能约束；不引入概率分布或现代标准合规结论。

articles.title: Both Spacers Passed, but Together They Were 0.1 Millimeter Too Wide
articles.summary: Thirty lamps are waiting to be shipped, but two individually acceptable spacers jam in the third hinge. Lin Yue measures each piece, then the space they take up together.
storyParagraphs: At 17:00, the courier is due to collect thirty folding reading lamps. Lin Yue is assembling the third lamp when the hinge suddenly refuses to slide into place. She removes the two aluminum spacers. There are no burrs on their edges, and caliper measurements show that both fall within the drawing's allowed range of 50±0.2 mm. Each part is acceptable on its own, so why do the two jam when placed together?

The previous lamp design used only one of these spacers at each location, so keeping each individual part within range was usually enough for assembly. The new version is the first to place two side by side in the same slot. Lin Yue measures the troublesome pair again: one is close to 50.2 mm and the other is also close to 50.2 mm. She measures the slot width as well: 100.3 mm.

Neither spacer is individually outside its limit, but 50.2+50.2=100.4 mm, which is 0.1 mm wider than the slot. She takes a compliant 49.9 mm spacer from the parts tray and pairs it with one of the 50.2 mm pieces, giving a total of 100.1 mm. That pair slides into the assembly successfully. She writes the two dimensions on one line, adds their combined length at the end, and puts the sheet beside the original individual inspection records.

More than twenty lamps are still waiting, and Lin Yue cannot assume that every piece will happen to find a suitable partner. This batch contains more than eighty already accepted spacers in stock, while thirty lamps require only sixty. She and a colleague remeasure the whole tray, sort the pieces into compartments, and then trial-fit them pair by pair. They actually find enough combinations for all thirty lamps; individually acceptable pieces that cannot easily be paired with the remaining stock for this slot are left in a separate box.

The workaround saves the day's shipment, but parts meant to be picked freely now have to be measured, paired, and trial-fitted, adding more than forty minutes to the batch. The design team records the 100.3 mm slot and the two 50±0.2 mm spacers for discussion in the next drawing revision rather than simply demanding that every dimension be tightened indefinitely. When the courier arrives, all thirty lamps are closed. The two 50.2 mm spacers on the inspection table are still individually compliant, but they sit together in a small bag labeled “combined length 100.4 mm.”
articles.overall: This article uses an idealized one-dimensional assembly to introduce engineering tolerance: individual parts can each lie within their allowed ranges without guaranteeing that the combined dimensions will fit the available assembly space. In a worst-case combination, deviations can accumulate in the same direction. Selective pairing can rescue a particular batch, but it does not create unrestricted interchangeability among all compliant parts.
explanationParagraphs: A tolerance allows an actual dimension to vary within a specified range. When several dimensions add along the same assembly direction, every individual part can be compliant while the combined dimension still exceeds the functional limit.

Minimal example: if each of two parts is 50±0.2 mm, each can range from 49.8 to 50.2 mm, so the ideal one-dimensional combined range is 99.6–100.4 mm. If the fixed slot width is 100.3 mm, the maximum combination of 100.4 mm exceeds it by 0.1 mm.

module.intro: First see why two individually compliant parts can still fail together, then check how their allowed variations accumulate in a one-dimensional extreme case.
module.diagramTitle: If Each Spacer Is Acceptable, Why Can Two Together Still Exceed 100.3 Millimeters?
diagramSteps: Each spacer is allowed to be 50±0.2 mm, giving an individual range of 49.8–50.2 mm
With two spacers side by side along the same direction, the minimum ideal combined length is 49.8+49.8=99.6 mm
The maximum ideal combined length is 50.2+50.2=100.4 mm
The ideal fixed slot width in this article is 100.3 mm, so the maximum combination exceeds it by 0.1 mm
For the day's batch, actual measurement and pair-by-pair trial fitting produce enough combinations, but do not restore unrestricted interchangeability
diagramStepNotes: This example covers only one-dimensional addition of dimensions, not complete geometric tolerancing.
The 100.3 mm value is treated as an ideal fixed slot width in this article; variation in the slot itself is not modeled.
The worst case combines allowed extreme values and does not assume that errors naturally cancel.
Combined length not exceeding slot width is only the simplified fit condition in this article and does not by itself guarantee complete hinge performance.
Selective pairing adds measurement, sorting, and trial fitting. Only the selected combinations have been checked; new pairings need another fit check.
mapping: Two 50.2 mm spacers → individually compliant pieces whose combined length reaches the 100.4 mm maximum.
100.3 mm fixed slot → the functional space limit in this one-dimensional teaching example.
49.9 mm paired with 50.2 mm → an actual 100.1 mm combination that fits successfully.
Sorted stock compartments → the extra work required for selective pairing that day.
module.boundary: This article uses a clearly defined one-dimensional dimension range and an ideal fixed slot width to show how dimensional variation can accumulate in a worst-case combination. Real assemblies can also involve slot tolerances, geometric error, clearance, surface condition, and other functional requirements, so “combined length no greater than slot width” does not by itself establish that the complete hinge is acceptable. Selective pairing is also not the same as designing for unrestricted interchangeability, and the example does not imply that all tolerances should simply be tightened.
module.reflection: If the two parts are still each allowed to be 50±0.2 mm but the fixed slot is changed to 100.5 mm, can the one-dimensional worst-case combination still exceed the slot because of length alone?

references.citation: Sudarsan, R., Roy, U., Narahari, Y., Sriram, R. D., Lyons, K. W., & Pramanik, N. (2000, May). Information Models for Design Tolerancing: From Conceptual to the Detail Design. NISTIR6524.
references.use: Supports the idea that assembly function can depend on accumulated dimensional variation across multiple components and that one-dimensional worst-case analysis can test functional constraints by combining allowed extreme values. No probability distribution or current standards-compliance claim is introduced.
